thread:
sam_support: customer (Ledgerly) hit a production failure — our runtime returned an Invalid JSON error for their fn call payload and the downstream billing service rejected because transferId was missing. customer says it worked yesterday.

alex_support: can you paste the raw request/response we received? request_id? any headers (content-type, sdk version)?

sam_support: request id 8f3a2c1e, route /v1/generate (hosted), SDK v1.4.0. attaching snippets below. response body is literally: `Error parsing JSON: Unexpected token '"' at position 0` but customer shows the model returned an object with keys but missing `transferId`.

sam_support: REQ (redacted headers):
```
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer ***
X-Redwood-Route: ledgerly-ingest
{
  "model": "open-32k-qa",
  "json_mode": "structured",
  "function": "createTransfer",
  "input": {"amount": 1200, "currency": "USD", "memo": "invoice 453"}
}
```

sam_support: RESP (truncated):
```
200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "function_call": {
    "name": "createTransfer",
    "arguments": "{\"amount\":1200, \"currency\":\"USD\", \"memo\":\"invoice 453\" }"
  }
}
```

josh_eng: looks like arguments were returned as a string (stringified JSON) and missing transferId key. that can cause downstream deserialization + schema validation to fail. two hypotheses: (1) model returned a string for `arguments` (double encoding) or (2) our json_mode handler failed to coerce/parse because it saw mismatched type (string vs object) and fell back to returning the raw string.

maya_research: we recently merged a generator patch that changes how function_call.arguments are emitted for very short outputs (to avoid leaking tokens). iirc there was a fallback that returns raw text if top-level tokenization looks ambiguous. could be related.

alex_support: customer says they started seeing this after we rolled runtime 2026-03-15. their traffic shows ~0.8% of calls to createTransfer now rejecting with schema errors; previously <0.01%.

josh_eng: can you repro locally with the exact model and the patch? sam, can you forward a full request_id logs (llog) including kernel version? deploy-bot should have the rollout details.

deploy-bot: rollout redwood-runtime/2026-03-15 (gk-4.12) -> deployed to hosted-us-east-1 (canary 10%, global 100%).

sam_support: pasted full logs to thread: `https://internal.logs/8f3a2c1e` (redacted). notable: our json-mode parser attempted JSON.parse on `arguments` and threw: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '"' at position 0` then we propagated an internal parse error to customer.

josh_eng: quick repro I ran with model weights locally: when the model emits `"{\"amount\":1200,\"currency\":\"USD\"}"` (i.e., with surrounding quotes) our parser tries JSON.parse and fails because it expects an object, not a quoted string. we should attempt a safe double-parse: if value is a string, try JSON.parse(value) and validate schema.

maya_research: agreed, but that risks silently accepting intentionally stringified payloads in some corner cases. alternative: strict mode + explicit diagnostic to caller: respond with parse_error but include both raw and attempted-parsed forms for easier customer recovery. for now, a pragmatic fix: auto-unquote then parse for `function_call.arguments` only when json_mode=structured and content-type application/json.

alex_support: customer urgently: their billing pipeline rejects transfers without transferId which causes failed settlements. they want a mitigation now — any temporary workaround?

josh_eng: mitigation options: (A) server-side hotfix to try double-parse then insert null transferId placeholder and return a 422 with clear message, (B) a tenant-level route fallback: route their traffic to pre-rollout runtime (gk-4.11) for 24-48h, (C) tell customer to change their client to validate and retry when parse failure occurs. (A) is fastest and transparent.

maya_research: +1 for (B) if we can flip their route quickly — lowest risk. (A) is ok as an emergency patch but we need a proper fix in the runtime for solidity.

sam_support: Ledgerly prefers a quick fix at our side. can we switch them back to 4.11?

deploy-bot: routing change request created: route=ledgerly-ingest, target-runtime=redwood-runtime/2026-02-28 (gk-4.11), ETA 12min to cutover.

josh_eng: I'll draft the emergency patch: behavior: if `function_call.arguments` is a string and looks like JSON (starts with `"{"` or `{`), attempt JSON.parse twice (unquote then parse). if parse succeeds, validate against declared function schema. log both raw and parsed to debug fields. will push as hotfix to canary.

alex_support: thank you. also creating a billing support ticket and will notify Ledgerly of the route rollback.

maya_research: long-term action items: (1) add unit tests for stringified arguments + nested arrays, (2) add a runtime flag to control tolerant parsing, (3) audit last two runtime commits that touched generator fallback heuristics.

sam_support: Ledgerly confirms they see no more failed transfers after the route cutover. marking customer as informed.

josh_eng: pushing patch to canary now, will monitor parse-error rate metric.

deploy-bot: canary patch deployed to hosted-us-east-1. metric: function_arguments_parse_errors dropped from 0.78% -> 0.02% in 9m.

alex_support: closing escalation ticket once we have a postmortem and followups. tagging eng for postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
notes: customer impact: missed transferId causing billing rejects; mitigation: route rollback + hotfix; root cause suspected generator fallback -> stringified arguments
